statusText:
Nothing has traded. The CME weekend halt still governs the published state: NQ futures have not quoted since Friday 14 August and Globex does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, about eight and a half hours from this run. Tail is 15%, the action is EA_ON and the status is green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the last observed path was benign.

The marginal news this hour runs the other way from last hour's reading, and Stress rises from 78% to 81% because of it. Two things changed. First, the Sunday flow turned kinetic again: the IDF struck southern Gaza near Khan Younis at about 11:56 UTC, reportedly hitting a tent and injuring displaced people, then struck Nuseirat in central Gaza at about 13:12 UTC targeting an operative, with several injuries reported. Last hour's assessment recorded no new kinetic escalation since Saturday; that is no longer accurate, and this hour corrects it.

Second, and more consequential for a market that has to reopen, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent signposted an unprecedented Iran economic package for the coming week. Speaking on Friday he said Washington would apply measures "like have never been seen in the history of the economic isolation of a country," combined with a continued Hormuz blockade keeping anything from moving in or out of Iranian ports, and told markets to watch for announcements next week. That is a confirmed, high-impact, unscheduled catalyst with a direct oil transmission channel, landing inside the coming week and possibly within hours of the restart. It is exactly the kind of credible unresolved second information wave the contract treats as an amplifier.

Against that sits a genuine diplomatic channel: a Hamas delegation met Egypt's intelligence chief Hassan Rashad on postwar implementation, with talks involving US officials and the Board of Peace planned around Jared Kushner's regional visit. Escalation and de-escalation are running at once. The contract is explicit that a conflicting signal set should raise Stress rather than Tail, and that is precisely what has been done here.
recommendation:
Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 15% maps to EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always.

The roughly 22:00 UTC Globex restart is the only checkpoint inside this forecast window, and the danger window stays anchored to it at 21:55-00:00 UTC, 23:55-02:00 Berlin. That is deliberately narrower than a whole-session shutdown: the risk is concentrated in the gap itself and the first two hours of thin Asian-transition liquidity. A full weekend of Gaza, Lebanon and Hormuz headlines, plus a signposted US sanctions package, has to clear into a single restart against a market that closed with implied volatility near the bottom of its 52-week range.

Forecast Tail drifts 15% to 19% through the remaining halt, steps to 21% at 21:00 UTC and peaks at 27% and 26% across the first two hours of live quoting - orange, block new base entries - before easing through the watch band and returning to green at 05:00 UTC Monday.

This is general market-risk assessment for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and it is not a recommendation to place any trade.
headline: CME weekend halt holds with about eight and a half hours to the Globex restart: Stress rises to 81% as Sunday turns kinetic again with two fresh IDF strikes in Gaza and Bessent's unprecedented Iran economic package is signposted for the coming week - Tail stays low at 15%, EA_ON and green, Confidence 77%
body:
Observed reference levels, all from Friday 14 August's close because nothing has traded since, and all re-verified from primary quote pages this hour. NQU26 settled at 30,141.75, down 46.75 points or 0.15%, opening at 30,210.75 against a 30,188.50 previous close and holding a 254-point range of 30,028.50 to 30,283.00 on 397,964 contracts. Investing.com still marks the contract Closed as of 14/08. It finished mid-range, roughly 2.7% below the 52-week high of 30,975.50 and far above the 22,961.50 low. There is no persistent directional efficiency in that, no shallow-pullback extension, no repeated failed retracement and no close near an extreme - the four things the contract requires before Tail belongs above 25%.

Volatility and rates, re-read this hour. VIX closed at 14.25, down 0.38 or 2.60%, day range 14.18 to 14.72, previous close 14.63, against a 52-week range of 13.38 to 35.30 - near the bottom of that range but not the low of 2026. The 2-year yield finished at 4.171%, up 3.1bp, day range 4.098 to 4.178; the 10-year at 4.696%, up 5.5bp, day range 4.625 to 4.700. That is a modest bear-steepening, not a cross-asset stress impulse. Low implied volatility into an unpriced restart is a thin cushion - a Stress statement, not a Tail one.

Equities and breadth from Friday. The Nasdaq Composite closed 26,729.16, down 0.28%; the S&P 500 7,785 and the Dow 53,732, both off about 0.2%, while the Russell 2000 rose 0.51% to 3,068, a fresh record - its third all-time high of the week. On the week the S&P added 0.4% and the Nasdaq 0.1% while the Dow fell 0.6%. A small-cap record set on a day the Nasdaq fell is broadening, not the narrow mega-cap leadership that typically precedes a one-way index break. Semiconductors were dispersed rather than aligned, with Broadcom down 5.9% and Intel 2% against AMD up 6.5% and Micron 2.3%, and dispersion inside the complex is the opposite of the alignment that would manufacture index-level one-way structure.

Oil and the Iran file, which is where this hour's new information sits. WTI is $82.40, up $1.15 or 1.42% on Friday, roughly 5% on the week, 3.52% on the month and 32.95% year on year; Brent $88.52, up $1.45 or 1.67%, and 34.43% year on year. Trading Economics attributes the weekly gain directly to Washington increasing economic pressure on Iran to reopen the strait, with the IEA warning of the widest global supply deficit in five years. The strait has been effectively shut since late February. Iran and Oman describe their vessel-movement talks as in final stages, but Araghchi says there are no active US-Iran negotiations and Tehran will not reopen until Washington "corrects its behavior," demanding sanctions relief, release of frozen assets and compensation. UKMTO reports shipping still at reduced levels with harassment activity continuing.

The new escalation vector is economic rather than kinetic. Bessent's package, promised for the coming week, sits on top of a blockade that has already cost Tehran about $4.8 billion in oil revenue, alongside reporting that Iran is planning to block US and Israeli ships from the waterway. US Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper visited the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Arabian Sea today; the carrier has been on station over 240 days supporting the port blockade and is due to be relieved by the USS George Washington. None of that is priced, because there is no venue open to price it.

Today's kinetic flow, from the Times of Israel liveblog. Two IDF strikes inside Gaza: Khan Younis in the south at about 11:56 UTC, with reports of a tent hit and displaced people injured, and Nuseirat in central Gaza at about 13:12 UTC targeting an operative, with several injuries. These follow Saturday's Israeli strikes on south Lebanon that killed 11 - the deadliest day since the June ceasefire, with a second senior Hezbollah commander identified among the dead and Defence Minister Katz vowing to settle scores - and the Gaza tank incident the IDF called a grave truce violation. Iran's parliament separately approved a bill criminalising contact with hostile media, carrying six months to two years in prison, a hardening signal at the margin.

Friday's macro still deserves to be carried forward. July retail sales fell 0.6%, the worst print since May 2025, and preliminary consumer sentiment came in at 51.0 against 54.5 expected. Equities took this benignly because it cut perceived odds of a September Fed hike, but a weakening consumer is a real seed for a growth scare and is part of why Stress sits in the extreme band while Tail does not.

Calendar, re-verified against Trading Economics this hour. The seven-day US list is front-loaded with housing and survey data, with FOMC Minutes on Wednesday 19 August at 18:00 UTC, jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed index on Thursday, and the S&P Global flash PMIs on Friday 21 August as the high-impact anchors. Industrial production is restored to the calendar this hour at 13:15 UTC Tuesday, high impact: it was omitted from recent runs because sources disagreed on the release time, and Trading Economics now gives a time matching the standard 09:15 Eastern release, so the uncertainty that justified omission is resolved. Jackson Hole falls on 27-29 August, outside this window, with Kevin Warsh due to give his first keynote as Fed chair on 28 August, and Nvidia earnings land the week after next - the two largest scheduled catalysts both sit just beyond the seven-day horizon.

Evidence quality. Confidence 77%. Futures levels, VIX, both Treasury yields, oil, the seven-day calendar and today's Middle East flow were read directly from primary pages this hour and are mutually consistent, and the industrial-production timing ambiguity was resolved rather than carried. Four fetches were refused this run - Reuters markets was blocked outright, CNBC's US 10-year quote page and its Iran carrier article both returned 403, and an Al Jazeera liveblog URL 404'd - and each was replaced from an alternative primary source, so no input was lost, though the Bessent quotes reach this assessment through search results over Friday reporting rather than a directly fetched article, which is the weakest link in the chain and is why Confidence is 77 rather than higher. The one irreducible gap remains that no live price path exists at all. During a scheduled venue halt that absence is a certain, known fact rather than an unreliable reading, which is why it caps Confidence in the low end of the high band rather than pushing it down.

lookbackSummary:
The trailing 24 hours run from 13:00 UTC Saturday to 12:00 UTC Sunday and sit entirely inside the CME weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours and the outcome was identical each time: EA_ON, green, dominantMode mixed. Tail never left the low band, drifting 10% to 14%. Stress carried all the movement, running 54, 55, 56, 58, 57, 60, 62, 65, 67, 67, 68, 70, 71, 73, 74, 75, then dipping to 70 and climbing 71, 71, 78, 79, then 78, 80 and 78. Confidence rose almost monotonically from 61% to 76%.

Three features of that track matter for reading the current hour. First, the entire Stress climb from 54 to the high seventies happened across a market that never quoted once. Part of it is genuine - Saturday's south-Lebanon strikes were new information - but part is a re-reading of a static evidence set as the reopen approaches, and that component should not be extrapolated mechanically.

Second, last hour tested exactly that and cut Stress from 80 to 78 on the grounds that no new kinetic escalation had occurred and a diplomatic channel was opening. This hour that judgement has to be partly reversed: two IDF strikes landed inside Gaza during the 11:00 and 13:00 UTC hours, and the Bessent package for the coming week surfaced as a distinct, larger catalyst. Stress moves back up to 81. The oscillation from 80 to 78 to 81 is the honest signature of genuinely conflicting inputs, not drift.

Third, the near-monotonic Confidence rise from 61% to 76% is genuine and continues to 77%. Successive hours added primary-source coverage of levels, volatility, rates, oil, breadth and the calendar even though the price path stayed unavailable. Tail's 10-to-14 drift across the whole window is the smallest movement in the set, which is the correct behaviour when the input that drives Tail - observed price path - has been absent for every single slot.
outlookSummary:
The next 24 hours end at 12:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC Globex restart and the first fourteen hours of live quoting sit inside the window. Tail stays in the low band for the eight remaining halt slots, drifting 15% to 19%, then steps to 21% at 21:00 UTC and peaks at 27% and 26% across the first two hours of live quoting before easing through 24%, 23%, 22%, 21% and 20% and returning to 19% and green at 05:00 UTC Monday, settling at 17% through the European morning. Forecast status is yellow at 21:00 UTC, orange at 22:00 and 23:00 UTC, then yellow through 04:00 UTC Monday and green thereafter.

That orange is conditional risk about the reopen, not an assertion that a one-way path has been observed. The reasoning is mechanical: a full weekend of unpriced Gaza, Lebanon and Hormuz headlines, plus a US sanctions package explicitly promised for the coming week, has to clear into a single restart in thin liquidity, against a market whose implied volatility closed near the bottom of its 52-week range. The peak is one point higher than last hour's forecast for the same slots because the Bessent catalyst was not in the previous reckoning. If the gap is small and mean-reverting within the first hour, these forecast numbers will prove too high and the next assessments should say so plainly.

Stress rises from 81% to a peak of 88% at the restart, then decays to 76% by 11:00 UTC Monday as the weekend stack is absorbed, ticking back to 77% for the final slot which contains the 12:30 UTC Empire State release. Confidence dips to 74% through the last hours of the halt as Friday's evidence ages, then rises sharply to 85-87% once live quoting restores the price path that is the single missing input. dominantMode is mixed throughout except for event/whipsaw across the four hours spanning the restart.

No high-impact scheduled US macro release falls inside this window - Empire State at 12:30 UTC Monday is medium impact and sits in the final slot, and the FOMC Minutes, jobless claims and flash PMIs are Wednesday through Friday. The restart itself is therefore the only genuine checkpoint in the forecast. The unscheduled Iran announcement is the wildcard: it has no timestamp, which is why it is reflected in the Stress path rather than in a second danger window.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour. CME is shut and no venue quotes NQ or the NAS100 CFD, so a pathological one-way price path cannot form - Tail 15% describes a frozen tape, not a calm one. Stress rises to 81% because the marginal news this hour turned escalatory again: two fresh IDF strikes inside Gaza today, and Bessent's unprecedented Iran economic package explicitly signposted for the coming week.

Roughly eight and a half hours to the Globex restart. No observable price evidence can arrive during this hour; only headline flow moves the assessment, and the Sunday flow has been running kinetic rather than diplomatic since midday UTC.

Tail edges to 16% purely because the reopen is nearer, not because anything has been observed. Stress 82% as the unpriced stack keeps accumulating - Gaza strikes, a signposted sanctions package and a closed Hormuz all still waiting for a venue to price them.
European Sunday afternoon. Friday's closes are now past 48 hours old, so Confidence begins drifting down while the price-path gap stays absolute. Still low-band Tail, still EA_ON and green.

Five hours out. Any Sunday-evening statement from Washington on the Iran measures now lands close enough to the restart to feed the gap directly, which is why Stress keeps climbing while Tail holds in the low band.

Tail 17%, Stress 83%. The last quiet stretch before positioning into the reopen begins. A market that closed with VIX at 14.25, near the bottom of its 52-week range, has thin cushion against a weekend of headlines it has had no mechanism to price.
